objective: Issue #4: identify up to three initial administrative problem signals across at least two industries without proposing a startup or fabricating customer evidence.
summary: Three candidate problems, two industries, four primary agency sources. Construction has an explicitly weekly task and an agency burden estimate; medical authorization and remittance workflows have substantial existing standardization. These are discovery signals, not validated commercial opportunities.
questions: What recurring administrative work is documented?
What existing tools or policy changes undermine a new-product thesis?
What high-value uncertainty should the next session resolve?

findings.text: DOL requires weekly reporting for covered contractors and provides detailed labor-classification, wage and fringe-benefit instructions.
The WH-347 information collection has an agency average burden estimate of 55 minutes; no small-firm distribution or avoidable-cost estimate was established.
CMS recognizes prior-authorization burden and describes API and operational requirements within a limited payer/non-drug scope.
Medicare remittances involve multiple adjustment levels, but CMS already describes automatic posting through ERA and free viewing tools.

Construction payroll export exceptions are the preferred next desk-research target because the recurring task is clear and a public-documentation comparison can cheaply falsify a generic automation thesis. This is a prioritization judgment, not proof of founder fit.

contradictory_findings.text: WH-347 is optional; reporting scope is restricted, and current payroll exports may already solve the work. The last point remains an untested hypothesis.
Payer API requirements and existing ERA automation challenge undifferentiated medical administration products. Neither page establishes the remaining gap for small practices.

unresolved_questions: All willingness-to-pay, buyer-access and small-business-specific pain questions remain unknown.
No vendor pricing, customer interviews, market sizes, or source-independent customer corroboration were collected.
Sources are four documents from two agencies, not four independent customer-demand studies.
Publication dates for three guidance pages are unknown; source access is dated, and rule implementation was not independently verified.
conclusions: Complete as a bounded discovery scan only. Keep all three problems at discovery/evidence-collected depth; create no opportunity record or commercial recommendation. Prefer one targeted construction competitor/workaround investigation next. Do not contact customers or begin product development.
next_steps: Compare existing certified-payroll exports and project-input workflows in public documentation; seek dated first-hand small-subcontractor evidence of residual friction.
If the gap is absent or already solved, retain these records and deprioritize rather than inventing a solution.
title: First discovery scan: construction reporting and medical payer administration

history.reason: Initial public-source discovery for issue #4; no customer interviews or commercial validation.
